lessons.title: Right triangles and calculator modes
lessons.objective: Use right-triangle geometry and side ratios, recover acute angles, and keep angle units and calculator modes consistent.
lessons.why: Restore the connection between a right-triangle picture, its ratios, and the calculator inputs that represent those ratios. These skills support component calculations, periodic signals, and geometry in later engineering work.
recall: Find the right angle first: the opposite side is the hypotenuse. Opposite and adjacent legs are named relative to the selected acute angle. Sine uses opposite/hypotenuse, cosine adjacent/hypotenuse, and tangent opposite/adjacent.

Use a positive square root for a length. A half turn is 180 degrees or pi radians; convert the angle before evaluating a trigonometric function. An inverse ratio recovers an acute angle only when you interpret the calculator output in the requested unit.
lessons.retrieval: Sketch a right triangle with legs 5 and 12. Name the hypotenuse, find the smaller acute angle, and explain how to evaluate the same angle in DEG and RAD modes.
